subject.title: feat: trace Claude Code CLI model calls

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `model.call.*` as an individual provider-request contract, or intentionally broaden it to include opaque aggregate CLI turns?
rationale: The Claude CLI does not expose its native Anthropic request boundaries, so code alone cannot make the synthetic turn both useful and semantically equivalent to existing model-call events; the permanent public telemetry unit requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve per-call semantics
options.body: Emit Claude CLI lifecycle under harness/run or a distinct CLI-turn span and leave `model.call.*` for observed provider requests.

options.title: Broaden the contract
options.body: Accept synthetic aggregate turns as model calls, then explicitly document and test the mixed telemetry units and downstream metric implications.

options.title: Pause CLI model spans
options.body: Keep only harness/run telemetry until Claude exposes trustworthy request-level boundaries or a separate span contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Preserve per-call semantics
recommendation.body: Emit Claude CLI lifecycle under harness/run or a distinct CLI-turn span and leave `model.call.*` for observed provider requests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on OTLP trace correlation makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the exported-span contract.
